items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: A fellow by the name of Belton Everett. And I worked with him

ctx.x: Yeah, this was -- no, I would say this would -- say about 1930, '31, and it was really rough, really rough. So then, I met some musicians from Pueblo, Colorado, and so they formed a little band, so I worked with them for awhile. A fellow by the name of Belton Everett. And I worked with him, because there was another saxophone player in the town, so they took the rhythm section and some others, and we worked with them around Pueblo and all of that. And he gave us a place to say and things like that.

And then I finally found that I had an auntie there, and she worked for a country club, so I didn't have to worry about nothing to eat. I was straight there, you know. So after I left -- I mean, I stayed there, and then finally I got ajob with the Walkathons. Remember the Walkathons?
